newsitem.title: USA: Arrest in JonBenet case will take 'long time'-police.
newsitem.headline: Arrest in JonBenet case will take 'long time'-police.

text.p: A police spokeswoman said on Thursday an arrest was unlikely in the murder of 6-year-old JonBenet Ramsey for "a long time" due to the circumstantial nature of the evidence in the case.

But she said police in the 14-week-old investigation still expected to make an arrest. "Police are not willing to concede at this point that there may never be an arrest," said Leslie Aaholm, spokeswoman for the Boulder police at a weekly news briefing.
"I would suggest it would continue to be a long time (before an arrest is made)," Aaholm said.

Friday will mark the 100th day since the body of the little girl, who was a beauty pageant winner, was found by her father in a windowless basement room in the family's posh Boulder home. The body was found some eight hours after her mother said she had found a ramson note demanding $118,000.
No arrests have been made and no suspects named in the investigation.
She said police were anxious to talk with JonBenet's parents, John and Patricia Ramsey. The Ramseys have not had a formal interview with the police.
Aaholm said because the case will likely be based on circumstantial evidence it may be some time before it is solved.
DNA testing was expected to begin this week and would take up to six weeks to be completed, she said.

The testing at the commercial laboratory Cellmark Diagnostics in Maryland was held up while the Ramseys considered an offer from the district attorney's office to have a representative view the testing. They declined the offer.
Aaholm said the DNA results would be significant, but would only constitute a piece in the puzzle, along with handwriting analysis and interviews with many people who knew the child.
The weekly news briefings will be discontinued and police will call media conferences if they have something significant to announce, although this would not necessarily be an arrest, she said.
